stem: Zubin packs a tiffin in three stages: first he picks one of 4 rice options, then one of 3 dals, then one of 2 sweets. Every rice–dal–sweet triple is allowed.

parts.text: Which claim correctly counts the tiffin combinations?

options.text: Count only the 4 rice options, because the later stages do not change the total.
The 2 sweets produce the 4 rice options, so start from sweets and ignore the rice and dal choices.
Count only tiffins that use the first rice option, so the total is $1\times3\times2=6$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Choices made in stages multiply: 4 rice options times 3 dals times 2 sweets gives 24 allowed tiffins.

teacher.key_rationale: Multi-stage combinations multiply the per-stage counts: 4×3×2=24. Dropping later stages omits required choices. Treating sweets as producing rice reverses the stages. Counting only the first rice option excludes the other stated rice choices.
